name: L-arginine
short: Lowers blood pressure (about 6 mmHg systolic in a meta-analysis); short-term use may cause gastrointestinal and cardiovascular adverse effects.
text: A meta-analysis of 22 randomised trials found that oral L-arginine lowered systolic blood pressure by about 6.4 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure by about 2.6 mmHg, in people with normal and with high blood pressure. A systematic review of safety in healthy adults concluded that short-term arginine supplementation may cause adverse gastrointestinal and cardiovascular effects. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
